summary: Delivers the digital experience through which students can discover, pursue, evidence and gain recognition for King’s Edge opportunities as the first substantive native product domain within the Digital Student Experience Hub.
detailSummary:
The King’s Edge Digital Experience delivers the student-facing capabilities needed to make the King’s Edge proposition navigable, personalised and usable. Students will be able to discover relevant opportunities, connect them to their aspirations, plan participation, manage activity, capture evidence, reflect on development and gain recognition for what they have achieved.

These requirements are being delivered directly on the shared Digital Student Experience Hub foundations rather than through a separate long-term Edge portal or interim app. King’s Edge is the first substantive native product domain through which the shared architecture, product capability and reusable experience patterns are established and tested.

The first priority is a controlled replatform of the existing Edge service, preserving service continuity and verified feature parity without waiting for the wider Student Systems and Data programme to complete. The product then develops through digital badging, multi-event programmes and pathways, King’s Canvas, project-based learning tools and provider-managed spaces. These capabilities are progressively brought together into a coherent Edge experience and then increasingly reuse common Hub capabilities as the wider Hub matures.

The result should deliver immediate value to Edge while strengthening shared capabilities that can subsequently support other student journeys.

caseForChange.problem:
King’s offers a wide range of experiences, activities and development opportunities, but students cannot currently navigate them as a coherent developmental journey. Opportunities are distributed across providers, systems and communications, and access depends too heavily on prior knowledge, confidence and networks.

King’s Edge intensifies the need for digital discovery, planning, participation, reflection, evidence and recognition. Delivering these requirements through a standalone long-term Edge destination would duplicate capabilities that are also valuable across the wider student experience.
caseForChange.opportunity:
King’s Edge provides a substantive, comparatively well-defined product domain through which the Digital Student Experience Hub can be established by doing real delivery. The Edge replatform can create immediate student value while testing shared application foundations, product practices, identity, navigation, orchestration, telemetry and reusable interaction patterns.

As the wider Hub matures, Edge can increasingly reuse common capabilities while retaining ownership of its distinctive proposition, opportunity offer, curation, developmental journeys and recognition model.
caseForChange.whyNow:
The existing King’s Edge platform needs to be replatformed and the programme has an immediate pipeline of richer product requirements. This creates a practical opportunity to ensure the investment contributes directly to the long-term Digital Student Experience Hub rather than creating another transitional destination.

The Edge replatform is sufficiently self-contained to proceed without waiting for completion of 1.2 Student Systems and Data, while still aligning specific authoritative-data and interface requirements with that programme.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
Students encounter King’s Edge as a coherent developmental experience within the Digital Student Experience Hub. They can discover opportunities, participate in programmes and projects, plan development through King’s Canvas, capture evidence and gain recognition through connected journeys.

By June 2029, Edge operates as a mature native product domain within the shared Hub, increasingly reusing common application capabilities while concentrating Edge-specific development on the quality of its proposition, opportunity discovery, developmental journeys, evidence and recognition. Product development continues beyond mobilisation where live evidence justifies it.

benefits.title: More students discover and access relevant opportunities
benefits.statement: A coherent and personalised route helps students find opportunities that fit their interests, circumstances, development needs and aspirations.
benefits.beneficiary: All students, particularly those less connected to informal opportunity networks
benefits.realisationPeriod: From release of discovery and recommendation capabilities
benefits.successLooksLike: A broader and more representative range of students discover and progress into relevant opportunities, with less reliance on chance or insider knowledge.

benefits.title: Students pursue development more intentionally
benefits.statement: Students can connect aspirations, plans and participation, helping them make more purposeful choices and sustain engagement across their time at King’s.
benefits.realisationPeriod: From implementation of planning and participation journeys
benefits.successLooksLike: Students use the environment to identify goals, select appropriate next steps and connect separate experiences into a meaningful developmental journey.

benefits.title: Students can evidence and articulate what they have developed
benefits.statement: Evidence capture, reflection and recognition help students understand and communicate the capabilities and impact developed through their King’s experience.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, graduates and prospective employers or partners
benefits.realisationPeriod: From implementation of evidence and recognition capabilities, strengthening over time
benefits.successLooksLike: Students maintain credible evidence of development, receive appropriate recognition and can articulate their skills and experience with greater confidence and specificity.

steps.title: Lock the Edge replatform scope and migration plan
steps.summary: From September to November 2026, confirm the current service capabilities to preserve, the agreed Year One product boundary, migration and service-continuity approach, and the boundary between Edge-specific functionality and shared Hub foundations.

steps.title: Replatform the existing King’s Edge app
steps.summary: Rebuild the existing King’s Edge app on the agreed Azure and shared-application foundations between November 2026 and the end of January 2027. Achieve verified feature parity before cutover and align specific authoritative-data and interface requirements with Student Systems and Data without waiting for the wider 1.2 programme to complete.

steps.title: Digital Badge Management Infrastructure
steps.summary: From February to April 2027, deliver the in-house badge-management infrastructure and the migration and cutover required to replace Accredible safely.

steps.title: Multi-event Activity and Pathway Management
steps.summary: From February to April 2027, extend the replatformed Edge service to manage linked programmes, multi-session participation, completion rules and curated developmental pathways.

steps.title: King’s Canvas prototype
steps.summary: During May and June 2027, develop and test a bounded working King’s Canvas prototype that helps students articulate needs and aspirations, form a revisitable plan and connect to relevant opportunities and pathways.

steps.title: Project-based Learning Delivery Tools
steps.summary: From June to August 2027, develop the first tools for structured project-based learning, including briefs, project spaces, milestones, submissions, outputs, evidence and reporting.

steps.title: Provider Curation and Managed Spaces
steps.summary: During August and September 2027, enable approved internal providers to manage and curate their offer within King’s Edge through delegated roles and governed provider spaces.

steps.title: King’s Canvas beta and opportunity matching
steps.summary: From October to December 2027, develop Canvas into a controlled beta and test how plans connect to opportunities, programmes, pathways and projects.

steps.title: Integrated King’s Edge release
steps.summary: During January and February 2028, bring the replatformed app, badges, programmes and pathways, project tools, provider spaces, Canvas beta and evidence records together as one coherent and supportable King’s Edge experience.

steps.title: Product operations and service stabilisation
steps.summary: From March to June 2028, stabilise the integrated service and establish routine product, support, release and operational practices.

steps.title: Personalised planning, progression and reflection
steps.summary: Use live evidence from July to December 2028 to strengthen movement from planning into activity, progression into deeper experiences, and completion into reflection, evidence and recognition.

steps.title: King’s Edge in the shared student app
steps.summary: During January to June 2029, make King’s Edge fully native to the shared Digital Student Experience Hub home, navigation, profile, search, communications and common interaction patterns while retaining ownership of the Edge proposition and developmental model.

steps.title: Mature King’s Edge product domain
steps.summary: After the three-year mobilisation, operate and improve King’s Edge as a mature product domain inside the Digital Student Experience Hub, focusing ongoing Edge-specific development on opportunity discovery, connected developmental journeys, evidence and recognition.
